items.title: An open subscheme of a locally Noetherian scheme is scheme theoretically dense if and only if it contains all embedded points, if and only if it contains all associated points
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states a three-way equivalence for an open subscheme U of a locally Noetherian X: scheme theoretic density, density plus containment of all embedded points, and containment of all associated points (statement lines 443-449). The work is a reduction plus an algebraic re-reading: the author first passes to X = Spec(A) with A Noetherian, uses quasi-compactness of U to write it as D(f_1) union ... union D(f_n), and then replaces the geometric conditions by statements about the single ring map A -> A_{f_1} x ... x A_{f_n} and about the associated primes of A (proof lines 453-462). The two non-obvious steps are reading density as containment of the minimal primes and invoking that the associated primes are exactly the minimal primes together with the embedded ones (proof lines 471-476), and closing the cycle by the injectivity of A into the product of its localisations at the associated primes (proof lines 479-484). This is H2: standard localisation machinery, but four separate implications, each needing its own translation rather than a citation.
